Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

replayr 0.4.0

Initial release.

  • Import console and computer input recordings from current and historical emulator formats, including TAS editor projects and ZIP members.
  • Store digital controls in compact logical arrays, with stable control IDs, readable labels, source metadata, and separate numeric channels.
  • Name button columns and numeric channels by key in every accessor, so that "a" and "left_x" select the same control and stick axis in every format; button_layout() and channel_layout() list the labels of the recording.
  • Name the controls of the console or cabinet by key as well: system_channels() has reset, power, pause and coin_1 in every format that records them, and system_layout() lists the labels of the recording.
  • List the formats with their readers and emulators through supported_formats(details = TRUE): 37 file extensions in 33 formats, with the format whose file structure an extension has. recording_format() says as which format a file is read, and so which files of a folder are recordings.
  • Read a recording under another extension: read_movie() recognises the formats that have a signature by their content, and format names the format in every other case.
  • Report platform, video standard, frame rate, duration and rerecord count under one name each with recording_info(), and the time of each observation with observation_time().
  • Provide summary(), as.data.frame() and [ methods for recordings: held observations and activations per control, one row per observation, and selection of observations that keeps the class.
  • Support independent left and right stick representations: four directions, eight directions, angle, or angle and magnitude. Source X/Y values remain available in every mode.
  • Take the default deadzone from the controller and not from the file format: 0.125 for the sticks of Nintendo’s consoles, 0.25 for other sticks.
  • Retain stick clicks, light-gun controls, mouse movement, keypad controls, touchscreens, keyboards, motion sensors, and separately recorded emulator and cabinet controls.
  • Read the BK2 recordings of Gym Retro with read_bk2().
  • Return the text that the author of a FinalBurn Alpha recording entered when recording, in movie$header$metadata.
  • Keep in the header what a recording says about the ROM or disc it was made with: the CRC32 and internal name of a Snes9x or ZSNES ROM, with the katakana of Japanese names; the header and global checksums of a Game Boy ROM and the game code of a Game Boy Advance ROM; the header CRC, country code and version of a Nintendo 64 ROM; the MD5 of a Dolphin disc image; and the IDs of the PlayStation discs played, in the order they were inserted. header$SHA1Kind says whether the hash BizHawk wrote under SHA1 is a SHA1, an MD5 or a CRC32.
  • Read the demonstration files of the Atari Grand Challenge and Atari-HEAD data sets (Atari 2600) with read_txt(). Each frame’s action becomes the five controls of the joystick. The states of the game that the files also hold (score, reward, episode) are not input and are not read. Both are .txt files, which read_movie() tells apart by their first line; a trial of Atari-HEAD can be read out of the archive of its game.
  • Read GoldSrc demos (Half-Life, Counter-Strike 1.x and other games of the engine, from the engine versions of 2001 on) with read_dem(): the 16 actions of each command, the movement and the view angles it asks for, and the console commands of the demo.
  • Read Doom-engine demos of Doom, Heretic and Hexen, from Doom 1.2 to MBF21 and dsda-doom, with their game actions under IDs of their own.
  • Preserve multi-controller M64 and DTM files as ordered poll streams when port labels are unavailable; accept a verified repeating port order for player assignment.
  • Refuse a file that is not of a reader’s format, with a message that names the problem; the FM2 reader requires the version 3 line that FCEUX requires. A path that is no file is reported as “File not found”.
  • Include original artificial samples, source-defined regression fixtures, article examples, and their deterministic generators.

Developed by Thorben Pelzer.
